text:
Ren: Quick postmortem note from today's rk3b-ptq bring-up on holdout. NDCG@10 +0.019, MRR@10 -0.041. Putting initial findings here.
Kai: Thanks. Same pattern we've seen. Do we have run ids and artifact links?
Ren: Baseline run://2026-03-12/rk3b-fp16 (sha: a1b2c3d4). PTQ run://2026-03-29/rk3b-ptq (sha: e5f6g7h8). Artifacts: s3://eval/artifacts/1791230000/.
Maya: Any differences in the holdout sample? small composition shifts can bias MRR.
Ren: Holdout composition parity check shows +3.0% short queries (<=5 tokens) vs baseline. But we also found serializer parity issues: legacy_html vs compact serializer produced ~2.1% candidate text diffs.
Kai: 2.1% is enough to move top1 around. Did you run per-query top1 compare?
Ren: Yes. Per-query compare: top1 flip rate = 5.9% (full holdout). Top1 flips concentrated in short queries and in items with anchors.
Maya: For quant angle, small score compression can shuffle ties. What's the score delta distribution near top1?
Ren: Many flips where baseline score diff ~0.0005-0.003. Quantized scores compress dynamic range, so anchor term becomes more influential.
Kai: Two-pronged mitigation: 1) enforce serializer parity in onboarding (normalize/unescape/trim) 2) add config mapping for quant variants: scale anchor_weight by 0.95 and enable stable tiebreaker for |delta|<1e-3.
Maya: Agree. Also run a seed-robustness check on calibration: PTQ calib seeds [7,42,99] and compare per-query flips. If seed variance dominates, we need larger calib set.
Ren: Ran seeds 7/42/99 on 20k sample. Flip rate varied by ~0.6 percentage points but aggregate MRR delta persisted. So seed noise is small contributor, not root cause.
Kai: Good to know. Did you test anchor_weight sweep?
Ren: Anchor sweep on 20k sample: weight 0.9 -> MRR delta -0.013, 0.95 -> -0.008, 1.0 -> -0.041. 0.95 looks like best tradeoff.
Maya: And stable-tiebreaker effect?
Ren: Enabling stable doc_id tiebreak when |score_a-score_b|<1e-3 reduced top1 flips from 5.9% -> 1.7% on the sample and improved MRR delta to -0.006.
Kai: Let's land two small changes behind flags: serializer parity enforce + quant-config mapping (anchor_scale=0.95, soft_tiebreak=stable). Add a fast-sample check in CI: top1_flip_rate < 2% and MRR_delta > -0.01 on 10k sample.
Maya: Also add a pre-onboard parity script that computes a normalized hash for candidates so serializer diffs are flagged automatically. I can PR a small tool.
Ren: I'll attach diffs to the PR. CI note: ci-bot, please create gating job using the parity script and the fast-sample eval.
ci-bot: New pipeline created: ml-onboard-parity-and-sample-check. Gate rules: parity_diff < 0.5% AND top1_flip_rate < 2% OR manual review.
eval-bot: Quick-run completed on 10k sample with quant-config: NDCG@10 +0.018, MRR@10 -0.007, top1_flip 1.5%. Artifacts: s3://eval/artifacts/1791230000/sample-run.
Kai: Nice. If full holdout with these settings holds, we can merge config mapping and ship model. Keep the changes configurable per model tag.
Maya: One more suggestion: when reporting to PMs, show both NDCG and MRR with cohort breakdown (short/medium/long queries + anchor/no-anchor). That avoids surprise from aggregate-only reports.
Ren: Agreed. I'll run full holdout with the config and upload cohort breakdown. Posting results when done.
Maya: Thanks everyone. Small wins but useful to codify parity checks so future bring-ups are faster.
Ren: Full holdout finished: with anchor_scale=0.95 + stable-tiebreak, final metrics NDCG@10 0.754 -> 0.772 (+0.018), MRR@10 0.489 -> 0.485 (-0.004). Uploading artifacts to the PR and closing the loop.
Kai: Great outcome. Ship behind flag, monitor top1 online telemetry for a week. :thumbsup:
